exposure: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) severity (mild vs. severe)
outcome: Maternal outcomes (pregnancy-induced hypertension, gestational diabetes, spontaneous preterm labor, need for induction, cholestasis symptoms, bile acid levels, liver aminotransferases)
Perinatal outcomes (fetal distress, stillbirths, gestational period at presentation)
cohort: 375 pregnant patients diagnosed with Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy (ICP) (serum bile acids >= 10 mmol/l), with gestational pruritus patients serving as controls.
finding: Severe Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy is significantly associated with higher risks of gestational diabetes, pregnancy-induced hypertension, preterm labor, fetal distress, and stillbirths, while Ursodeoxycholic acid effectively ameliorates cholestasis symptoms and biochemical markers.
mod_finding: Severe ICP was associated with a higher frequency of induction of labor compared to mild ICP.
